query: How should we define 'module completion', 'goal-creation', and 'goal-follow-through' in analytics to distinguish initiation from maintenance?

response.query: How should we define 'module completion', 'goal-creation', and 'goal-follow-through' in analytics to distinguish initiation from maintenance?
response.answer: Module completion is the initiation of a defined task or goal. Goal-creation is establishing a target. Goal-follow-through is completing the task or achieving the target. These terms distinguish between starting and finishing a goal.

results.title: Customer Journey Map: Definition & Process — updated 2026 | IxDF
results.content: # Customer Journey Maps. ## What are Customer Journey Maps? What is the customer journey map in design thinking? In design thinking, a customer journey map visually represents a user's interactions with a product or service over time. A customer journey map and a user journey map are tools to understand the experience of users or customers with a product or service. Customer journey maps and service blueprints are tools to understand and improve the experience of the users or customers with a product or service. If the massive metropolis of New York City can be simplified to a useful transit map, if a 20-year-old question can be answered by a map of one soccer game, and if NASA was able to use maps to successfully send three humans on a 900,000-mile round-trip to the moon, then surely you can use a journey map to help your design team create a better user experience!
